event_summary: 1897年、23歳のラフマニノフが発表した交響曲第1番の初演は、不出来な指揮も重なり大失敗に終わった。彼は深く傷つき、1917年の亡命の際に楽譜をロシアに残したまま二度と演奏しようとしなかったが、死後の1944年に各楽器のパート譜だけが偶然発見され、翌1945年モスクワで甦った。

portrait_prompt: Illustrated cinematic portrait of Russian composer Sergei Rachmaninoff, based on the well-known photographic portrait of him as a mature man: short dark brown hair cropped close, receding at the temples with a high prominent forehead, deep-set pale grey-blue eyes under slightly heavy brows, long straight nose, strong angular jaw, clean-shaven face with a stern, serious, almost melancholic expression and tightly set thin lips. Fair, smooth skin with subtle age lines at the eyes. He wears a dark formal suit jacket over a crisp white dress shirt and a dark necktie, exactly as in the reference image, with no extra jewelry or ornamentation. Bust-to-shoulder composition, facing slightly toward the viewer. Painterly oil-portrait rendering, cinematic soft lighting, not photorealistic. Background is a plain, muted dark olive-brown tone with minimal gradation, no vignette, no border, no frame, artwork extending fully to all four edges of the canvas. No text, no signature.

middle_slides.text: 1897年、23歳のセルゲイ・ラフマニノフは渾身の交響曲第1番を発表したが、指揮の出来も悪く初演は惨憺たる失敗に終わった。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustration of a young Sergei Rachmaninoff at age 23 in 1897: short dark brown hair with a high forehead, deep-set grey-blue eyes, long straight nose, clean-shaven stern face but with slightly smoother, more youthful features than his later years. He sits slumped backstage in a dim St. Petersburg concert hall, elbows on knees, head bowed into one hand in visible anguish and humiliation, dressed in a formal dark tailcoat and white shirt. In the blurred background, orchestra musicians are packing up their instruments and a conductor's empty podium is visible under fading stage light, conveying the disastrous failure of the premiere. Warm but somber candle-lit tones, painterly brushwork, not photorealistic, no text.

middle_slides.text: 深く傷ついたラフマニノフは、1917年に祖国を離れる際この交響曲の楽譜をロシアに残していき、曲は長い沈黙の中に消えていった。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustration of Sergei Rachmaninoff around age 44 in 1917: short dark hair receding at the temples, high forehead, deep-set grey-blue eyes, long straight nose, clean-shaven stern face matching his known portrait likeness, now with a touch more maturity in his expression. He stands at a snowy Russian train station platform at dusk, wearing a long dark winter coat and hat, suitcase in hand, glancing back over his shoulder toward a modest writing desk visible through a lit window behind him where a thick bound musical score lies abandoned on the desk. His body and face both turned back toward the window in a natural three-quarter pose, expression somber and resolute, evoking departure and leaving something precious behind. Muted blue-grey winter palette, painterly brushwork, not photorealistic, no text.

middle_slides.text: 1944年、彼の死の翌年、紛失していた総譜の代わりに各楽器のパート譜が、レニングラード音楽院の資料庫で偶然発見されたのだった。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustration set in a dusty Leningrad Conservatory archive room in 1944: tall wooden shelves packed with yellowed folders and bound manuscripts, soft beams of light filtering through a high window illuminating floating dust particles. A pair of hands (no visible face) carefully lifts a faded stack of individual orchestral part-books tied with string from a forgotten box. On the wall nearby hangs a small framed portrait of Sergei Rachmaninoff with his short dark receding hair, deep-set grey-blue eyes, long straight nose, and stern clean-shaven face matching his known likeness, now rendered with a touch of care to suggest it as a memorial image after his death, soft shadows under the eyes suggesting the solemnity of remembrance rather than any change in his facial structure. Warm sepia and amber tones, painterly brushwork, not photorealistic, no text.

middle_slides.text: 1945年、死後わずか2年で交響曲第1番はモスクワで甦り、再評価の末、今では世界中のオーケストラが演奏する名曲となった。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustration of a grand, ornate Moscow concert hall in 1945, full orchestra performing on a brightly lit stage with a conductor mid-gesture, bows raised, music stands full of sheet music, and an enthralled audience seated in rows below, warm golden stage lighting filling the hall. Above the stage, a large framed portrait of Sergei Rachmaninoff is displayed in tribute, showing his short dark receding hair, high forehead, deep-set grey-blue eyes, long straight nose, and stern clean-shaven face exactly matching his known likeness, honoring his memory as his symphony is triumphantly revived. Rich warm reds and golds, painterly brushwork, cinematic grandeur, not photorealistic, no text.

fb_caption:
なぜラフマニノフは、渾身の交響曲を自ら封印してしまったのでしょうか。23歳での初演大失敗から半世紀近くを経て、楽譜なき名曲は思わぬ形で蘇ります。🎵

「忙しい大人のためのクラシック音楽ノート」では、忙しい日々の合間に、
ほんの数分だけ立ち止まりたくなる、クラシック音楽の物語を発信しています。
指揮者マエストロ・ノートが案内する、作曲家たちの知られざる人生の
ドラマ——栄光の裏にあった挫折、常識をくつがえす意外な真実——を、
毎日少しずつお届けしています。

難しい知識は必要ありません。ただ、物語として楽しんでいただければ、
それだけで十分です。

YouTubeでは、この作曲家の物語を動画でもお届けしています。https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yTmvr3Gl02M
